evidence.ref: Trusted backend contract: the DeepFM trainer consumes target['main'] plus target['engagement_aux'] with hp.aux_weight=0.2

expected_observation: If the weak hate task causes negative transfer, the replacement will improve trusted primary while leaving inference inputs and feature dimensions unchanged; training metadata should show the same four-head shape but a changed auxiliary-target checksum.

experiment_contract.claim: The experiment tests only whether profile-enter is a better fourth shared-representation auxiliary target than hate at the unchanged auxiliary weight.
experiment_contract.expected_observable: The engagement_aux shape remains unchanged, exactly one target column checksum changes from is_hate to is_profile_enter, and resulting model predictions differ despite identical inference features.
experiment_contract.falsification_condition: Invalidate the run if no unique hate column is found; otherwise reject the hypothesis if trusted marginal portfolio primary is non-positive or the paired acceptance gate fails.
forbidden_shortcuts: Do not expose profile-enter, hate, or any post-exposure feedback as an inference feature.
Do not change auxiliary weight, head count, architecture, epochs, or learning rate.
Do not assume a column position without verifying it against the train-only is_hate array.
Do not replace multiple auxiliary tasks.
required_components: Use DV.train_targets for train-only is_hate and is_profile_enter arrays.
Verify which existing engagement_aux column equals is_hate before replacement.
Replace exactly one auxiliary column and preserve the main long_view target.
Keep hp.aux_weight=0.2 and all model, feature, training, and prediction settings unchanged.
Run DV.assert_trainable on the new auxiliary target.

fallback: If the hate-column assertion fails, mark the proposal incompatible rather than guessing a column; if it runs but fails trusted acceptance, restore SO.build_target unchanged.
hypothesis: Replacing the extremely sparse, essentially uncorrelated hate auxiliary with the denser profile-enter signal will reduce negative transfer and improve w002's long_view ranking and marginal portfolio contribution.
implementation_plan: In build_target, first obtain the existing pointwise_engagement_mtl target from SO.build_target. Load train-only is_hate and is_profile_enter through DV.train_targets. Identify and assert the single engagement_aux column exactly matching is_hate on selected train rows, copy the auxiliary matrix, and replace only that column with is_profile_enter. Preserve target['main'], every other auxiliary column, model architecture, auxiliary weight, optimizer, and prediction path unchanged. Call DV.assert_trainable on the replacement target.
justification: At the fixed auxiliary weight of 0.2, an almost label-orthogonal event can inject noisy or conflicting shared-representation gradients. A denser auxiliary with a weak but positive relationship to long_view should provide more stable supervision while changing only one head's target, making the measured delta attributable to auxiliary-task selection rather than scalar tuning.
mechanism: replace weak hate auxiliary head with profile-enter supervision
observation: The exact train diagnostics report train_target_phi_with_long_view.is_hate=-0.003941107614124816 and train_target_rates.is_hate=0.0004206423208238981, versus train_target_phi_with_long_view.is_profile_enter=0.14612987498722513 and train_target_rates.is_profile_enter=0.02539102209073255. The profile-enter correlation is still weak because its absolute phi is below 0.2, but it is materially larger and the event is much denser.
research_nonuse_reason: This proposal is directly motivated by exact train-only target statistics and the current four-head target consumer. E003 tests a different auxiliary-weight transition on legal_rank_stack_v1, while no supplied research record evaluates replacing hate with profile-enter on this DeepFM parent.
risk: Profile-enter has only weak phi correlation with long_view and may still induce negative transfer.
The existing four auxiliary heads may not include hate, in which case the required uniqueness assertion will deliberately fail.
Profile-enter behavior may drift over the date split.
Previous target-block rollbacks indicate elevated empirical risk for auxiliary redesigns.
